references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.38(4), (6) and Fourth Schedule — overtime at 1.5× the hourly basic rate (12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44)); the rate for a non-workman is capped at the $2,600 salary level, $13.60 an hour (MOM, Changes to the Employment Act from 1 April 2019)
MOM, Hours of work, overtime and rest days — Part 4 coverage (read 2026-11-13)
references.quote: Part 4 of the Employment Act does not cover managers and executives. … You can claim overtime if you are: A non-workman earning a monthly basic salary of $2,600 or less. A workman earning a monthly basic salary of $4,500 or less.

description: Overtime on a working day, and rest-day hours past the normal day: 1.5 × the hourly basic rate (12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44)), capped at $13.60 an hour for a non-workman (EA s.38). Part 4 employees only (workman ≤ $4,500, other ≤ $2,600 basic a month; no manager or executive).

references.title: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations; MOM, Overtime for part-time employees — hours within a comparable full-timer’s normal hours are paid at the hourly basic rate

description: Part-time hours past the agreed day and up to the comparable full-timer’s day, at 1 × the hourly basic rate (PT Regulations).

references.title: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations; MOM, Overtime for part-time employees — hours beyond a comparable full-timer’s normal hours are paid at 1.5× the hourly basic rate

description: Part-time hours past the comparable full-timer’s day, at 1.5 × the hourly basic rate (PT Regulations).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.37(2)–(3) — rest-day work is half/one day’s basic pay at the employee’s request and one/two days’ at the employer’s request
MOM, Hours of work, overtime and rest days — Part 4 coverage (read 2026-11-13)
references.quote: Part 4 of the Employment Act does not cover managers and executives. … You can claim overtime if you are: A non-workman earning a monthly basic salary of $2,600 or less. A workman earning a monthly basic salary of $4,500 or less.

description: Work on a rest day, paid at the employer-request rate: one day’s basic pay for up to half the normal hours, two days’ above half (EA s.37(3)); the employer’s own hourly rest-day multiple where it pays more. Part 4 employees only.

references.title: MOM, Part-time employment: rest days — rest-day hours between the part-timer’s and full-time normal hours are paid at the hourly basic rate

description: Part-time hours past the agreed day and up to the comparable full-timer’s day, at 1 × the hourly basic rate on a rest day (PT Regulations).

references.title: MOM, Part-time employment: rest days — rest-day hours beyond full-time normal hours are paid at 1.5× the hourly basic rate

description: Part-time hours past the comparable full-timer’s day on a rest day, at 1.5 × the hourly basic rate (PT Regulations).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.88(4) — an employee required to work on a public holiday is paid an extra day's salary at the basic rate of pay (MOM, Public holidays: entitlement and pay)

description: A public holiday worked: one extra day’s basic pay for each holiday worked, on top of the salary (EA s.88(4)).
